title: AdaptiveKV: Accelerating KV Cache Offloading with a Bandwidth-Adaptive Memory Allocation Mechanism
summary: AdaptiveKV accelerates LLM inference by using a bandwidth-adaptive memory allocation mechanism for KV cache offloading across CXL-enabled memory pools. The method achieves a maximum speedup of 1.90× in LLM inference throughput compared to state-of-the-art strategies.

title: BlockServe: Block-Grained Continuous Batching for High-Throughput Diffusion LLM Serving
summary: BlockServe is a serving framework for diffusion LLMs that uses block-grained continuous batching and mixed-state execution to handle convergence heterogeneity, achieving up to 10.6x throughput improvement over prior baselines.

title: StreamDQ: Near-Memory Weight DeQuantization in Custom HBM for Scalable AI Inference Acceleration
summary: StreamDQ introduces near-memory weight dequantization in custom HBM to eliminate GPU-side overhead, achieving up to 7.08x speedup for mixed-precision GEMM and 2.20x higher decode throughput in end-to-end LLM inference.

title: General Non-Clairvoyant KV-Cache Scheduling via Regime-Aware Routing
summary: The paper introduces a non-clairvoyant scheduling algorithm for batched LLM inference that manages requests under a hard KV-cache memory budget to minimize total completion time. It provides the first constant-competitive algorithm for arbitrary prompt and response lengths using a novel regime-aware routing framework of specialized sub-schedulers.

title: Automated Tensor Scheduling for Hybrid CPU-GPU LLM Inference on Consumer Devices
summary: ATSInfer is a hybrid CPU-GPU inference system that performs tensor-granularity offloading combined with load-aware dynamic transfer and asynchronous coordination. The abstract reports up to 1.94x prefill throughput and 3.29x decode throughput improvements over existing systems on consumer devices.

title: Unlocking Parallelism in Autoregressive Language Models via Speculative Decoding with Progressive Tree Drafting
summary: Progressive Tree Drafting (PTD) uses a structured, guided parallel drafting strategy with a progressive tree structure and stepwise pruning to explore multiple paths in a single forward pass. The abstract claims PTD achieves up to 2x decoding speedup while remaining training-free and model-agnostic.

title: TIGER: Text-Conditioned Visual Gated Routing with Acceptance Alignment for Multimodal Speculative Decoding
summary: TIGER introduces a text-conditioned visual gated routing framework for multimodal speculative decoding that dynamically selects sparse visual tokens and applies acceptance-aligned policy training to the drafter. The method is evaluated under exact verifier-side speculative decoding, demonstrating gains in accepted prefix length and speculative speedup while maintaining downstream accuracy.

title: FastTPS: An Optimized Method for LLM Token Phase for AI accelerators
summary: FastTPS accelerates the token-phase in LLM inference via reloading-free KV Cache concatenation, optimized RoPE attention, and a fused MLP pipeline. The method achieves a 6x speedup and 93% peak memory bandwidth utilization on an AMD NPU during Phi3-mini inference.

title: HCRMap: Pressure-Aware Hot-Expert Residency Mapping for 3.5D MoE Chiplet Inference
summary: HCRMap proposes a pressure-aware hot-expert residency mapping framework for 3.5D MoE chiplet inference that dynamically manages expert replicas across memory tiers to mitigate communication and memory bottlenecks. Experiments show the method reduces end-to-end latency by up to 46.7% over baseline methods in both prefill and decode stages.

title: Less Experts, Faster Decoding: Cost-Aware Speculative Decoding for Mixture-of-Experts
summary: EcoSpec is a cost-aware speculative decoding framework for Mixture-of-Experts models that incorporates predicted marginal expert activation costs into draft tree selection to reduce expert scattering. Evaluated on large-scale MoE models, the method reduces active expert footprints and achieves up to 1.62x end-to-end decoding speedup.

title: Rethinking LLM Deployment for Intent-Based Serving
summary: MaverIQ is an intent-based LLM inference serving system that maps user intents to deployment configurations using lightweight fingerprints and analytical models to extrapolate latency and memory. The abstract reports that the system reduces profiling cost by 7-15x and operational cost by 3.8-8.3x compared to baselines.

title: The Economics of AI Decoding Chips: Rebalancing Compute, Capacity, and Bandwidth for Efficient LLM Inference
summary: The paper proposes a rebalanced LLM decoding hardware accelerator (Skymizer HTX-301) using commodity DDR5 memory instead of high-bandwidth memory to lower costs. It demonstrates end-to-end inference serving of DeepSeek-R1 671B at a deterministic 20.3 tokens per second for a fraction of the cost of standard GPU nodes.

title: Efficient and Privacy Aware Edge Cloud Collaborative Inference for Large Language Models
summary: The paper proposes a privacy-centric edge-cloud collaborative LLM inference framework where local endpoints perform speculative decoding and the cloud conducts token verification. It reports reducing per-token latency by up to 46.1% and downlink payloads by up to 67.4% over baseline split inference.

title: GigaWorld-Policy-0.5: A Faster and Stronger WAM Empowered by AutoResearch
summary: The method introduces a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that separates visual dynamics modeling from action generation to reduce active computation during action-only inference. The abstract reports that this approach preserves training benefits while achieving an 85 ms inference latency on a local RTX 4090 setup.

title: FlexiTensor: Adaptive Multi-Task Deployment of LLMs on Resource-Constrained Heterogeneous Edge Devices
summary: FlexiTensor is an offline planning and deployment system for LLM inference on heterogeneous edge devices that uses non-uniform tensor parallelism, quantization, and evolutionary scheduling to optimize latency under energy budgets. Evaluated on a physical testbed, it accelerates single-task inference by up to 50% and improves multi-task workflow speed by an average of 50%.

title: Smarter and Cheaper at Once: Byte-Exact KV-Cache Grafting Turns a Frozen Small Model into a Verified-Knowledge Flywheel
summary: The method grafts byte-exact key-value (KV) state artifacts into fresh inference contexts, achieving byte-for-byte identical logits to fresh computation. It reduces decode tokens by a factor of 6,574 and expands usable context to 2.8 million tokens at zero extra accelerator memory.

title: Seeing the End at Step Zero: Accelerating Diffusion MLLMs via MLP Sparsity-Aware Truncation
summary: Seer is a training-free framework that accelerates Diffusion MLLMs by detecting the semantic boundary at the first denoising step via MLP activation sparsity and truncating redundant suffixes. It improves batched serving throughput by up to 31x while maintaining or improving accuracy across 9 benchmarks.

title: D-cut: Adaptive Verification Depth Pruning for Batched Speculative Decoding
summary: D-Cut is an adaptive cross-request pruning method for batched speculative decoding that selects draft tokens based on confidence and a runtime cost model. Under high concurrency, it improves average speedup from 1.26x to 1.65x and achieves up to 3.0x speedup over autoregressive decoding on MoE models.

title: Scaling Attention Beyond GPUs for LLM Inference
summary: Beyond is a drop-in runtime that uses a smart offloading scheme and hybrid CPU-GPU attention to process oversized KV caches cooperatively during bandwidth-constrained decoding. It improves scalability, supports longer sequences and larger batch sizes, and outperforms existing sparse attention baselines in efficiency and accuracy.

title: Omnia: Efficient RAG Serving through Speculative Scheduling
summary: Omnia is a RAG serving system that uses chunk speculation with a two-level coarse-to-fine reranking architecture and backpressure-aware scheduling to overlap prefilling and decoding. It maintains near-lossless accuracy while increasing maximum request rate by 57% and reducing average end-to-end latency by 2.99x.

title: VarRate: Training-Free Variable-Rate KV Cache Compression for Long-Context LLMs
summary: VarRate is a training-free KV cache codec that assigns each token a variable low-rank budget based on query salience instead of evicting tokens. It stays within 0.8 points of the uncompressed model on LongBench at a 20% memory budget while significantly reducing prefill overhead.

title: RecGPT-V3 Technical Report
summary: The method introduces a Memory Hub for structured user memory and Latent Intent Reasoning to internalize verbose rationales into compact latent tokens. In large-scale online A/B tests, it cuts end-to-end serving resource consumption by 52.4% and output token cost by 200x while improving commercial metrics.

title: Every Microsecond Matters: Achieving Near Speed-of-Light Latency in GPU Collectives
summary: The method develops low-latency GPU collective communication kernels using barrier-free synchronization and multicast to approach the hardware speed-of-light lower bound. When integrated into LLM inference, these kernels improve inter-token latency and throughput while reducing collective overhead to within 7% of the absolute lower bound.

title: Agon: Competitive Cross-Model RL with Implicit Rival Grading of Reasoning
summary: Agon introduces a two-stage cascade where one model drafts a solution and another reads it to provide the final answer, using this setup for competitive cross-model RL. At inference, it doubles GRPO's pass@1 on the hard split of DeepMath with Qwen3 compared to GRPO alone.

title: FlashRT: Agent Harness for Guiding Agents to Deploy Real-Time Multimodal Applications
summary: FlashRT is an agent harness that guides coding agents to optimize multi-GPU deployments of multimodal applications. The abstract claims it achieves up to ~70x latency reduction and up to 3.6x throughput improvement across NVIDIA and AMD hardware, reducing latency by 65% for Qwen3-Omni compared to vLLM.

title: LMEdge: QoS-Aware LLM Inference Orchestration on Edge Clusters
summary: LMEdge is a QoS-aware orchestration service that uses machine learning predictors and a lightweight heuristic to dynamically select model configuration and execution placement for edge devices. Evaluated on a Kubernetes testbed with 57 instances, the method reduces latency, preserves accuracy, and improves resource utilization compared to baselines.

title: Transition-Aware Backend Dispatch for Edge LLM Inference
summary: The paper proposes a transition-aware backend dispatch approach that dynamically selects operators for edge LLM inference based on shape and backend-transition costs. Evaluated via trace replay, it reduces latency, energy, and energy-delay product by 17.4%, 14.4%, and 28.5% on average compared to the best static policy.

title: D-NOVA: In-Storage Retrieval Accelerator via Dual-Bound 3D NAND-Optimized Similarity Search with Vector Adaptation
summary: D-NOVA is a hardware-software co-designed in-storage accelerator that executes IVF-based retrieval pipelines directly within 3D NAND memory. It achieves up to 41.7x speedup and 71x energy efficiency over a CPU baseline, and 12.13x higher throughput than state-of-the-art in-storage RAG accelerators.

title: C$^2$KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference
summary: C2KV introduces a unified framework for non-prefix KV cache reuse that jointly optimizes extraction and concatenation using a lightweight sidecar extractor. It reduces KV cache storage and transfer costs, achieving up to a 17x inference speedup under long contexts while preserving generation quality.

title: Mage-Flow: An Efficient Native-Resolution Foundation Model for Image Generation and Editing
summary: The paper presents Mage-Flow, a compact 4B-scale visual generation stack using a lightweight VAE and CUDA kernel fusion to improve training and inference efficiency. It claims a 2.5x improvement in training throughput and reports that its Turbo variant achieves low-latency inference, generating a 1024x1024 image in 0.59 seconds on an A100 GPU.

title: Generative World Renderer at the Speed of Play
summary: The paper introduces AlayaRenderer-Flash, a real-time generative world renderer reformulated as a few-step autoregressive streaming model with lightweight distilled codecs. The method accelerates rendering from 0.56 FPS to 31.54 FPS, enabling a fully playable 30 FPS generative world.

title: InstantInfer: Enabling Fast LLM Cold Start with Communicating Finite Automata
summary: InstantInfer uses Communicating Finite Automata to safely refactor LLM inference components for concurrent execution and I/O merging, applying this to vLLM cold starts. The abstract reports up to 7.2x speedup for LLM cold-start acceleration across diverse GPUs, workloads, and scales.

title: ABot-World-0: Infinite Interactive World Rollout on a Single Desktop GPU
summary: The paper presents a streaming inference stack with efficient attention, memory-aware scheduling, and low-bit inference for a video world model. The system streams 720P video at up to 16 FPS on a single desktop GPU with 1.2s action-to-first-frame latency and approximately 19GiB peak VRAM.

title: AdaFlash: Adaptive Speculative Decoding via On-Policy Distilled Diffusion Drafters
summary: AdaFlash improves speculative decoding by using on-policy distillation to reduce variance in diffusion drafters and an adaptive length head to dynamically adjust candidate sequence length. The abstract reports that the method achieves up to approximately 66% higher throughput than previous state-of-the-art methods, with significant gains in high-concurrency scenarios.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models in Long Document Generation
summary: The paper proposes UASD-DLM, an uncertainty-aware inference scheduler that dynamically adjusts draft depth and context refresh policy for speculative decoding in diffusion language models. It demonstrates improved speed-memory trade-offs and recovery of technical-term accuracy over fixed-depth speculative decoding in a controlled CPU proxy benchmark.

title: FVAttn: Adaptive Sparse Attention with Runtime Load Balancing for Video Generation
summary: The paper introduces a training-free sparse attention system with runtime load balancing and slack-aware augmentation for video diffusion transformers. The method achieves a 4.41x attention speedup over FlashAttention and a 2.02--2.11x end-to-end DiT inference speedup with competitive video quality.

title: BaseRT: Advancing Best-in-Class LLM Inference with Apple M5 Neural Accelerators
summary: BaseRT is a native Metal inference runtime for Apple Silicon that utilizes M5 Neural Accelerators for compute-bound matrix multiplications. It demonstrates up to 6.4x higher prompt-processing throughput and up to 1.75x higher decode throughput compared to baseline runtimes across various LLM configurations.

title: SANA-Video 2.0: Hybrid Linear Attention with Attention Residuals for Efficient Video Generation
summary: SANA-Video 2.0 introduces a Hybrid Linear-Softmax Attention mechanism and Block Attention Residuals to reduce quadratic attention costs in video diffusion transformers. It achieves a 3.2x faster forward pass than a full-softmax baseline and a further 3.58x speedup via full-stack engine optimization, resulting in 120x faster generation than a competing model on a single H100.

title: Cross-Modal Variance-Aware KV Cache Optimization for Efficient Multimodal Long-Context Inference
summary: The method proposes a cross-modal query-position variance-aware KV cache optimization method for multimodal long-context inference that allocates visual KV cache budgets and prunes tokens. Evaluations on LLaVA-v1.5-7B show that retaining 20% of the visual KV cache reduces GPU memory from 1.28 GiB to 0.26 GiB and decoding latency from 100.28 ms/token to 92.85 ms/token while maintaining performance close to the full-cache reference.

title: PHONON: Silicon-Photonic Network-on-Interposer for Energy-Efficient and High Performance LLM Inferencing
summary: PHONON is a Silicon-Photonic Network-on-Interposer architecture that jointly optimizes compute and storage inter-chiplet communication for LLM inferencing. The abstract claims it reduces NoI latency and energy consumption by up to 9.4x and 28.4x respectively, while improving LLM-serving time-to-first-token by 1.48x and tokens/Joule by 28x.

title: LLM-Advisor: Dynamic Model Selection and Query Routing in Heterogeneous Multi-LLM Architectures
summary: The method introduces an adaptive framework for dynamic model evaluation and constraint-aware request routing across heterogeneous LLMs, evaluated on 1,000 queries to achieve a 42% reduction in inference cost and 35% latency decrease while retaining 94.6% task accuracy.

title: Unified Static-Dynamic Pruning for Efficient LLM Inference
summary: The paper presents SPDP, a unified static-dynamic pruning framework with co-designed GPU kernels and compressed formats for efficient LLM inference. Evaluated on inference-optimized GPUs, it achieves 1.24x-1.37x average speedup over state-of-the-art sparse frameworks while maintaining perplexity.

title: LayoutLite: Token-Level Implicit Layout Analysis for Efficient Document OCR
summary: LayoutLite is a lightweight plug-and-play module that accelerates VLM-based OCR by implicitly analyzing layout at the token level to remove low-information visual tokens before decoding. It reduces prefill latency, FLOPs, and KV cache memory by over 40% with negligible degradation in recognition quality under up to 50% token compression.

title: OmniScope: Modality-Decoupled Token Compression for Omnimodal Large Language Models
summary: OmniScope is a training-free token compression framework for omnimodal LLMs that decouples modality-specific salience estimates. It achieves up to a 3.53x prefill speedup and more than 15% GPU memory reduction at 25% token retention with only a 0.35-point drop in average accuracy.

title: Omni-Prune: Query-Aware Unified Token Pruning for Efficient Omnimodal Large Language Models
summary: Omni-Prune is a training-free, query-aware token pruning framework that removes redundant audio and video tokens in Omnimodal LLMs to reduce prefill latency and memory usage. The method delivers up to a 3.25x prefill speedup and 1.3x memory reduction while retaining over 99% of full-model performance.

title: Sol-Attn: Accelerating Video Generation Inference via On-the-Fly Attention Sparsification
summary: Sol-Attn accelerates video generation inference via training-free on-the-fly attention sparsification that dynamically selects critical key-value blocks. It achieves 2.1x and 2.3x end-to-end speedups for video generation and editing while preserving visual quality.

title: MAViE: A Multi-scale Adaptive Vision Encoder for Fine-grained Visual Perception and Efficient Multimodal Reasoning
summary: MAViE is a multi-scale adaptive vision encoder that performs question-conditioned token routing to reduce visual token context length. The method is evaluated on visual question answering benchmarks, demonstrating a reduction in visual tokens from 729 to 146 and a decrease in single-image time to first token from 228 ms to 129 ms.

title: DraftExpert: Expansion-Aware Self-Speculative Decoding for End-Device MoE Inference
summary: DraftExpert is an expansion-aware self-speculative decoding framework for expert-offloaded MoE inference that uses a lightweight draft expert verified by the target model. Across CPU-GPU and Flash-NPU offload settings, it raises draft acceptance to 84-87% and improves decode throughput by 1.45x on average.

title: Beyond Prefill-Decode Disaggregation: Dissecting LLM Inference for Heterogeneous Platforms via Dynamic Operator Scheduling
summary: DOPS is a hardware-aware framework that optimizes LLM inference across heterogeneous systems using a dynamic operator scheduler and a weight layout arbiter. Evaluated on systems with NPUs and PIM devices, the method achieves geometric-mean speedups of 1.20x to 2.23x over the prefill-decode disaggregation baseline, with an additional 1.28x to 1.33x speedup from the layout arbiter.

title: OmniDelta: Skill-Driven Budget Allocation for Token Compression in OmniLLMs
summary: OmniDelta is a training-free framework for token compression in omni-modal LLMs that dynamically allocates retention budgets across audio and video modalities based on query demands. Evaluated on Qwen2.5-Omni-7B at 25% token retention, the method reduces GPU memory by 22.0% and achieves a 1.64x end-to-end speedup over full-token inference.

title: AngelSpec: Towards Real-World High Performance Inference with Speculative Decoding
summary: AngelSpec is a unified training and inference framework for speculative decoding that co-specializes multi-token prediction and block-parallel diffusion drafters, dynamically reallocating verification compute across requests. It achieves a 1.98-2.40x speedup over autoregressive decoding and up to 11.8% higher throughput than the DFlash baseline.

title: TurboVLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Model at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with <1 GB VRAM
summary: TurboVLA reformulates the vision-language-action pathway into a direct mapping to reduce computational and memory overhead, achieving 31.2 ms inference latency and <1 GB VRAM on an RTX 4090.

title: Revisiting Lossy Verification in Speculative Decoding: Mechanisms, Trade-offs, and Failure Modes
summary: The paper presents a principled analysis and diagnostic evaluation framework for lossy verification methods in speculative decoding, classifying them into truncation-based and collaborative approaches. It identifies fundamental pitfalls in truncation-based methods and key principles for collaborative verification to prevent low-quality outputs.

title: MRCoder: An Efficient Context Selecting Approach for Repository-Level Code Generation
summary: MRCoder uses a lightweight draft model to select repository-level code contexts and employs a parallel verification strategy for final decoding. The method reduces token consumption by 30 to 50% and inference time by up to 52%.

title: Beyond KV Reconstruction: Functional Reconstruction for MLA Draft Models in Speculative Decoding
summary: The paper proposes a functional reconstruction method for converting MHA/GQA draft models to Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) to improve draft-token acceptance in speculative decoding. Evaluated across 192 configurations, the method materially improves acceptance in 37 of 64 matched task cells without decreasing overall performance.

title: Prox: Training-Free FFN Activation Sparsity via Approximate Intermediate-Channel Salience in LLMs
summary: Prox is a training-free activation sparsification framework for FFNs that uses input sparsity and quantized proxy weights to construct a shared mask, achieving up to a 1.99x end-to-end decoding speedup at 70% FFN sparsity.

title: Calibrate Before Reason: Robust Visual Token Reduction against Semantic Drift in VLMs
summary: CaRe is a training-free visual token reduction framework for VLMs that calibrates compact visual representations to preserve semantic fidelity. Evaluated across diverse benchmarks, it retains 96.4% of full-token performance while pruning 94.4% of visual tokens, achieving up to 2.30x faster end-to-end inference.

title: A Sparse Glimpse of the Whole: Train-Free Self-Speculative Decoding
summary: SparseSpec-L is a training-free self-speculative decoding framework that drafts from a target model using a dynamically sparsified, recallable KV cache and an entropy-based controller for speculation length. Evaluated on multiple long-context tasks, it demonstrates consistent end-to-end acceleration over autoregressive decoding while preserving the output distribution.

title: SmartGen: Seamless Disaggregated LLM Inference with Selective KV Cache Transfer
summary: SmartGen is a KV cache transfer engine that mitigates network bottlenecks in disaggregated LLM serving by selectively transferring essential KV cache entries across prefill and decoding nodes. The method reduces time-to-second-token by up to 4.3x compared to full KV cache transfer while maintaining comparable decoding performance.

title: WIDE: Boosting Adaptive LLM Inference via Token-level Dynamic Width Pruning
summary: WIDE is a token-level dynamic width pruning framework with a pruning-kernel co-design that enables efficient execution across different granularities. The method achieves up to 1.98x prefill and 4.95x decoding kernel-level speedups, along with 1.68x and 1.55x end-to-end acceleration.

title: Accelerating inference in genomic and proteomic foundation models via speculative decoding.
summary: Adapts speculative decoding to genomic and protein foundation models using a lightweight draft model to propose tokens and a larger target model to verify them in parallel. The method yields consistent speedups over key-value cached decoding, with maximum observed speedups reaching a 100% increase and average gains of 1.2x-1.4x across models without changing the target model's predictions.

title: ParaASR: Multi-Token Prediction for Fast and Long-Context LLM-Based Speech Recognition
summary: ParaASR uses Multi-Token Prediction to propose multiple future tokens and admits only the verified prefix into the transcript. It achieves an average accepted length of 5.0 out of 6 proposed tokens and a real-time factor as low as 0.0053.

title: SLIM: Saturation-Aware Lightweight Performance Modeling for LLM Serving
summary: The paper introduces SLIM, a semi-analytical performance model for LLM serving that predicts throughput and latency to advise batching configurations. The model successfully identifies up to 55 GB of avoidable GPU memory allocation for evaluated OPT models with minimal throughput loss.

title: Studying quantization trade-offs for efficient inference deployment in machine translation
summary: The paper studies quantization trade-offs and document-chunking strategies for efficient machine translation deployment. It demonstrates that combining W4A8 or W8A8 quantization with chunking improves the latency-throughput Pareto-curve under various workloads on A100 and H100 GPUs.

title: AdaMTP: An Adaptive Training Paradigm for Multi-Token Prediction
summary: AdaMTP proposes an adaptive training paradigm for multi-token prediction that aligns prediction horizons with intrinsic sequence predictability using entropy-based segmentation. It demonstrates improved task performance and inference speedup over standard MTP across multiple backbones.

title: CURE: Local Uncertainty Repair for Block-Parallel Speculative Decoding
summary: CURE introduces a budget-aware dynamic repair tree for block-parallel speculative decoding that identifies and repairs high-uncertainty draft tokens. It increases the average accepted length by 4.2-7.5% over baselines, yielding an end-to-end speedup of 2.66-3.49x over target-only decoding.

title: TrimMoE A communication aware and adaptive depth framework for distributed edge inference
summary: TrimMoE is a communication-aware framework for distributed edge inference that couples layer skipping, early exit, and expert selection to reduce MoE cross-server transmission. On a 10-server testbed, it reduces average latency by up to 62.8% while keeping task-quality degradation within a 2% bound.

title: Celty: SpMspV GPU Kernel and SIMT Co-Design for Efficient Dual-Sparse LLM Inference
summary: Celty is a co-designed sparse format, GPU kernel, and SIMT microarchitecture for efficient Sparse Matrix-Sparse Vector (spMspV) workloads in dual-sparse LLM inference. The proposed SIMT core achieves up to 5.3x speedup over cuBLAS at 70% dual-sparsity.

title: Bole: Efficient Tree Speculation for Hybrid-Attention Language Models
summary: Bole is a kernel-runtime co-design enabling efficient tree speculative decoding for hybrid-attention LLMs via a tree-structured recurrence and batch-wide verification. It accelerates linear-attention tree verification by 3.4-7.7x and delivers up to 4.72x offline decode throughput over autoregressive decoding.

title: PrefixPlace: Provable Prefix Key-Value Placement for Large Language Model Serving under Heterogeneous Compute and Transfer Costs
summary: PrefixPlace is an epoch-level planner for prefix KV-cache placement across heterogeneous workers, optimizing for compute and transfer costs. The method achieves near-optimal cost savings (40.3% over vLLM-APC in RAG replays) and scales to 50,000 nodes in 12.3 seconds.

title: Energy-Efficient LLM Serving via Disaggregated Attention--FFN and Flexible Frequency Scaling
summary: AFlex is a serving framework that jointly optimizes resource provisioning and GPU frequency scaling for disaggregated Attention-FFN execution using an interleaved A/F pipeline. It reduces energy per token by up to 49% over state-of-the-art disaggregated serving while satisfying latency SLOs.

title: Output-Aware Rotation for INT2 KV-Cache Quantization
summary: OptR is an output-aware rotation method for INT2 KV-cache quantization that minimizes post-attention output error by learning per-head orthogonal corrections. The method improves long-context retrieval and strengthens quantization while preserving the paged KV-cache format with negligible inference overhead.

title: LLM Serving in the Wild: An Empirical Study of Frameworks, Methods, and System Designs
summary: The paper empirically studies the adoption of LLM serving frameworks and methods in open-source systems, analyzing frameworks like vLLM and SGLang. The study characterizes framework popularity and serving-method usage across various repositories and deployment settings.

title: PI-Mem: Pushing Long-Context Reasoning to 3.6M Tokens with Parallel-Iterative Memory
summary: PI-Mem processes long-context chunks in parallel and iteratively refines a shared memory to avoid sequential bottlenecks. The method is evaluated on HotpotQA up to 3.6M tokens, demonstrating high accuracy and inference speedups of 6.1x and 2.1x.

title: RestoreKV: Recovering Full-Cache Behavior Under Aggressive Query-Agnostic KV Cache Eviction
summary: RestoreKV introduces learned restoration tokens that attend to the full KV cache during prefill to generate a compact restore cache, mitigating aggressive query-agnostic KV cache eviction. It improves 59 of 60 budget-matched settings across five eviction methods and reaches 86.4 RULER accuracy at 16x compression on the KVPress Benchmark with less than 0.5% one-time overhead.

title: Heterogeneity-Aware Microscaling for Efficient Low-Bit LLM Inference
summary: The paper introduces AdaMX, a heterogeneity-aware adaptive microscaling format and accelerator for low-bit LLM inference that selects precision-recovery schemes per block and per operand. Evaluated on a 22nm FD-SOI accelerator prototype, AdaMX removes up to 83% of the MXFP4 accuracy loss while lowering memory footprint and energy.

title: On Design Principles for Efficient Heterogeneous DRAM-PIM-GPU Systems
summary: The paper establishes design principles for heterogeneous DRAM-PIM-GPU systems to accelerate decode-phase LLM inference. It reveals that static power dominates efficiency and that workload mapping provides bounded end-to-end gains of up to 5.6%.

title: RAC: Reference-Aware Activation Compression for Communication-Efficient Split LLM Inference
summary: RAC is a reference-aware codec for split LLM inference that compresses boundary hidden states to reduce communication bottlenecks. It improves time to first token and time per output token ratios by 1.24-2.72x and 1.01-2.79x respectively across evaluated models while maintaining task quality.

title: EdgeXpert: An Edge Device for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference with Mixture-of-Experts and Speculative Decoding
summary: EdgeXpert is a software-hardware co-designed LLM accelerator that resolves incompatibilities between speculative decoding and mixture-of-experts via prompt-wise expert reuse and depth-aware expert coalescing. Evaluated on a 28nm chip at 800 MHz, it achieves up to 56.3% latency reduction and 44.1% energy reduction compared to prior works while maintaining near-baseline accuracy.

title: A Two-Tier Perspective on Inference-Time Parallelism in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
summary: The paper proposes TIPEX, a controllable execution framework that unifies replica and structural parallelism in multi-agent LLM systems to coordinate concurrent execution. Systematic experiments on the GAIA benchmark demonstrate that inference-time parallelism can significantly improve accuracy and reduce end-to-end latency at the cost of increased token consumption.

title: PaDoc: Layout-Grounded Parallel Decoding for Document Parsing
summary: PaDoc proposes a layout-grounded parallel decoding method for document parsing that branches regional content concurrently using masked parallel decoding and shared-prefix reuse in vLLM. Evaluated on an A800 GPU, it improves valid-page throughput by 67.4-118% and reduces P95 latency by 39.2-54.9% relative to a sequential baseline.

title: BALANCE: Hybrid Autoregressive-Speculative LLM Inference in Wireless Edge Networks
summary: BALANCE is a hybrid autoregressive-speculative decoding framework for edge networks that dynamically schedules users to either standard decoding or small language model drafting with target LLM verification to optimize resource allocation. Experiments demonstrate that the method consistently outperforms conventional autoregressive and speculative decoding by significantly improving task throughput.

title: LLM Inference Under Bursty Workload Distribution: Modifying the WAIT Algorithm
summary: The paper proposes a lightweight extension to the WAIT scheduling algorithm to adapt to time-varying, bursty request arrivals for LLM serving. Simulation-based evaluation demonstrates higher throughput than Sarathi-Serve, ORCA, and vLLM in low arrival-rate shift scenarios while maintaining comparable latency.

title: Routing LLM Inference to the Cleanest Grid in Real Time
summary: The paper presents a live validation of carbon-aware inference routing for multi-region GPU testbeds, using real-time marginal operating emissions rate (MOER) signals to steer request placement. In a primary modeled configuration, the method reduces modeled GPU-attributable operational emissions by 50.9% versus round-robin placement.

title: OrionInfer: Low-Overhead Parallelism Switching and Live Migration for Efficient LLM Serving
summary: OrionInfer is an LLM serving system that uses low-overhead parallelism switching and live migration to improve efficiency, evaluating the system's serving performance.

title: E<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$^{2}$</tex-math><alternatives><mml:math><mml:msup><mml:mrow/><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:msup></mml:math><inline-graphic xlink:href="feng-ieq1-3676689.gif"/></alternatives></inline-formula>LLM: Structure-Guided Efficient Inference for LLMs in Distributed Edge
summary: E^2LLM is a distributed inference framework that uses edge devices for structural planning and lightweight auxiliary models to generate segment-specific KV caches for collaborative parallel decoding. The framework achieves 74%-87.7% end-to-end latency reduction and 34.6%-72.2% communication overhead reduction compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

title: Token-Burst-Aware Capacity Planning for LLM Inference Services: Request Arrival, Token Demand, and Failure Risk Modeling from BurstGPT Traces
summary: The paper presents an integrated capacity planning pipeline for LLM inference services that forecasts token demand, detects bursts, and simulates capacity policies. Evaluated on BurstGPT traces, the method links demand forecasting to GPU counts, latency, batching, and memory pressure via Vidur replay to optimize serving efficiency.

title: Learning to Predict Middle-Layer Attention in MLLMs for Visual Token Prunin
summary: The method predicts middle-layer text-to-vision attention using a lightweight predictor to prune visual tokens before the first LLM layer, preserving 97.5% of performance with only 5.56% of visual tokens. The strongest result present in the abstract is a 3.09x end-to-end inference speedup.

title: Cascade: Exploiting SLO-Aware latency budget for fair and high goodput LLM inference serving
summary: Cascade is an LLM serving system that uses a per-request latency budget to jointly coordinate request scheduling and KV-cache management across the memory hierarchy. Evaluated on production traces, it improves SLO-satisfied goodput by up to 2.4x and reduces SLO violations by 40% relative to a baseline vLLM scheduler.

title: FutureBridge: Token Selection Beyond Local Preference in Collaborative Decoding
summary: FutureBridge introduces a token-level collaborative decoding method where a large model expands a candidate pool and a small model verifies tokens based on counterfactual reasoning support. It improves a Qwen3-1.7B SLM's Math Avg. by 35.1% relative to greedy decoding across five benchmarks.

title: RoRA: Role-Oriented Regional Allocation for Visual Token Pruning in MLLMs
summary: RoRA is a training-free visual token pruning framework that reduces KV-cache storage for multimodal LLMs. At a 66.7% pruning ratio, it reduces end-to-end inference time by 24.6% (a 1.33x speedup) over unpruned inference on an NVIDIA H800.

title: An AI4AI Framework for Visual Token Pruning
summary: AutoPrune is a training-free framework that uses LLMs to design visual-token pruning policies for multimodal LLMs via a domain-specific language. It preserves over 99% of full-token performance while removing 94.4% of visual tokens, reducing FLOPs by 9.9x and prefill latency by 6.4x.

title: OasisKV: Scaling In-Decode KV Cache Beyond HBM with Lookahead Sparse Prefetching
summary: OasisKV is a memory-centric inference system that uses lookahead tokens drafted via speculative decoding to accurately prefetch and stage sparse KV-cache entries from host/remote memory into HBM. It achieves up to 2.1x throughput over dense vLLM on multi-GPU long-context serving with minimal accuracy loss.
